lines.japanese: 祖母には「欠席」ではなく「遅刻」の連絡を入れてもらった。
lines.english: I have my grandmother call the school to say I'll be late, rather than absent.

lines.japanese: 彼女の勧めを受けて、学校へ行く前にクリニックへ寄ることになったからだ。
lines.english: At her suggestion, I'll stop by the clinic before going to school.

lines.japanese: 外出できるうちに今週分の診療を受けておいた方が良いと判断して、わざわざ電話で担当医に、突発の予約を入れられるか確認してくれたらしい。
lines.english: Apparently, she decided I should have this week's appointment while I was able to go out, and went to the trouble of calling my doctor to ask whether they could fit me in.

lines.japanese: 共働きの両親は私の病気について理解が浅いけど（親戚に怠け病とか根性なしと説明していたのを聞いたことがある）、祖母は店番の合間にせっせと本を読んだり、ときには診察に付きそってくれたりする。
lines.english: My parents, who both work, don't understand my illness very well. (I've heard them explain it to relatives as laziness or a lack of willpower.) But my grandmother diligently reads books between watching the shop, and sometimes comes with me to appointments.

lines.japanese: 大好きなおばあちゃん。だけど病状のひどいときには、そんな彼女の無償の優しささえ煩わしく感じてしまうのだ。
lines.english: I love my grandma. But when my condition is bad, even her kindness, given without asking anything in return, feels like a burden.

lines.japanese: 早く完治させたいとつくづく思う。
lines.english: I really want to get completely better soon.

lines.japanese: 「行ってきます」
lines.english: “I'm off.”

lines.japanese: いちご二粒とヨーグルトだけの朝食をとり、自信や勇気をもたらすというサンストーンをポケットに忍ばせて、店の玄関口から外へ出た。
lines.english: After a breakfast of just two strawberries and yogurt, I slip a sunstone, said to bring confidence and courage, into my pocket and leave through the shop entrance.

lines.japanese: 冬の朝の乾いた空気が頬を刺す。風の冷たさをまざまざと実感できるのは体調が良い証拠。
lines.english: The dry air of a winter morning stings my cheeks. Feeling the wind's cold so vividly is a sign that I'm doing well.

lines.japanese: 私の病気は医学的にも社会的にも精神的疾患に区分されているけれど、個人的にはしっくりいかない。
lines.english: Medically and socially, my illness is classified as a mental disorder, but personally, that doesn't sit right with me.

lines.japanese: 脳内物質が不足して、交感神経と副交感神経の均衡が崩れる──その結果として心身の活動低下を余儀なくされる。これと熱を出して寝込むことと、いったい何が違うんだろう。
lines.english: A shortage of chemicals in the brain upsets the balance between the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. As a result, mental and physical activity are forced to slow down. How is that any different from being laid up with a fever?

lines.japanese: でも、そんな風に不平を覚えるのも体調が良い証拠。
lines.english: But feeling disgruntled about it is another sign that I'm doing well.

lines.japanese: そんな今日の自分に安堵して、ほのかに嬉しくなってしまうのも体調が良い証拠。
lines.english: Feeling relieved about myself today, and a little happy, is another sign that I'm doing well.

lines.japanese: 喜怒哀楽が湧くのは健康の証。生きてるって素晴らしいな。
lines.english: Feeling joy, anger, sorrow, or pleasure is a sign of health. Being alive is wonderful.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: ちょっと前に見慣れた制服の背中。あれはたしかクラスの男子……名前、なんていったっけ？
lines.english: A little ahead, a familiar uniformed back. That's a boy in my class, I think... What was his name?

lines.japanese: 学級委員長の……はねだ、くん？　そうだ、たしか羽田君だ。
lines.english: The class president... Hane... da? Right. Haneda, I think.

lines.japanese: 私のクラスに私の名前をすぐに思いだせないひとは、たぶん大勢いると思う。病気のことがばれないように、いつも極力目立たないようにしているから。
lines.english: There are probably plenty of people in my class who wouldn't remember my name right away either. I always try to be as inconspicuous as possible so they won't find out about my illness.

lines.japanese: そうしてクラスの輪に近づかない私だから、こちらにとっても教室にはよく知らないひとだらけ。
lines.english: Since I stay outside the class circle, the classroom is full of people I don't know well either.

lines.japanese: ネット上の瑠樺には覚えきれないほどの薄い繋がりがたくさんあるけど、オフラインの山科京というのはそういう存在。
lines.english: Ruka online has more faint connections than she can keep track of. But that's what Miyako Yamashina offline is like.

lines.japanese: 私はいったん店へ入って、わけもなく前髪を直したり、陳列棚の商品に触れたりした。
lines.english: I go back into the shop, adjust my bangs for no reason, and touch things on the display shelves.

lines.japanese: 数十秒ほどの時を進めてから、また改めて外へ出る。
lines.english: After moving time forward by a few dozen seconds, I go outside again.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 同級生の背中はもう見えなくなっていた。
lines.english: My classmate's back is no longer in sight.

lines.japanese: ひと気のない住宅街を駅に向かって歩きながら、ＭＰ３プレイヤーを取りだした。
lines.english: Walking toward the station through the deserted residential streets, I take out my MP3 player.

lines.japanese: ディスプレイに表示されていたのは、初期ロックバードの『後ろを向いて歩こう』。まだ聴き手のほとんどがアナーキーな男の子だった時代の、ラウドなパンクロック。
lines.english: The display shows an early Rockbird song, ‘Let's Walk Looking Back.’ Loud punk rock from when most of their listeners were anarchic boys.

lines.japanese: イヤホンを手に握ったまま、再生ボタンを押してみる。激しく掻きならされたギターサウンドと、ボーカル御影クリヤの雄叫びじみた歌声がしゃりしゃりと溢れでてきた。
lines.english: Holding the earphones in my hand, I press play. Fiercely strummed guitars and the almost roaring voice of their singer, Kuriya Mikage, spill out in a tinny rush.

lines.japanese: 思わず顔をしかめた。駄目だ。とてもじゃないけど、こんな暴力的な音を受けいれられる状態じゃない。耳障りで頭が割れそうになる。
lines.english: I can't help grimacing. No. I'm in no state to take in sound this violent. It's so grating my head feels like it'll split.

lines.japanese: 急いで別の曲を探した。主張しない音がいい。イージーリスニングやケルト音楽のような、押しつけがましくない旋律にゆっくりと体を浸したい。
lines.english: I hurry to find another track. Something that doesn't insist on itself. I want to slowly immerse myself in an unobtrusive melody, like easy listening or Celtic music.

lines.japanese: 私は焦った。しゃりしゃりと高音域のノイズが侵食してくる。逃げられるわけでもないのに、自然と歩く速度が上がっていった。
lines.english: I grow anxious. Tinny, high-pitched noise keeps invading me. My pace naturally speeds up, though it's not as if I can run away.

lines.japanese: 「うるさいなあ」
lines.english: “So noisy.”

lines.japanese: 焦りと苛立ちに頭を掻きみだされながら親指を連打して（かちかちかちかち！）、ディスプレイに表示される候補曲を次々と送ってゆく。
lines.english: With anxiety and irritation clawing at my head, I hammer the button with my thumb—click, click, click, click!—sending one candidate track after another across the display.

lines.japanese: 「うるさいなあ、うるさいなあ」
lines.english: “So noisy, so noisy.”

lines.japanese: 思考がまとまらず、何を聴けばいいのか決めることができない。
lines.english: My thoughts won't come together. I can't decide what to listen to.

lines.japanese: 集中力の崩壊。判断力の融解。見慣れたはずのタイトルもただの文字列としか思えず、どんな楽曲が流れてくるのかイメージを結ばない。
lines.english: Concentration collapses. Judgment melts. Even titles I ought to know are only strings of letters. I can't form an image of the music they would bring.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、もうっ……！」
lines.english: “Oh, come on...!”

lines.japanese: 涙ぐみながら適当なところで再生ボタンを押した。しゃりしゃりが止んで、とつぜん沈黙が訪れた。
lines.english: Tears in my eyes, I press play at some arbitrary point. The tinny noise stops. Suddenly, silence.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……はあ……」
lines.english: “Haah... Haah...”

lines.japanese: 私は立ちどまった。自分の荒い呼吸音を聞きながら、恐る恐るイヤホンを耳に近付けた。すぅーっと、澄んだ木管楽器の吹鳴が沁みわたる。
lines.english: I stop walking. Listening to my own ragged breathing, I cautiously bring the earphones toward my ears. A clear woodwind note seeps gently through me.

lines.japanese: これは……ああ、あれだ……ふだんは就寝前の布団の中でしか聴かない室内楽団のアルバムだ。よかった、これにしよう。
lines.english: This is... Oh, that one... An album by a chamber ensemble I normally only listen to in bed before sleeping. Thank goodness. I'll go with this.

lines.japanese: 改めてイヤホンを両耳に装着し、目を閉じる。
lines.english: I put the earphones properly into both ears and close my eyes.

lines.japanese: 音の粒を転がすような可愛らしいピアノ。
lines.english: A charming piano, rolling little beads of sound.

lines.japanese: 緑の野に吹く穏やかな風に似たオーボエ。
lines.english: An oboe like a gentle wind across green fields.

lines.japanese: 両者が互いを愛でながら紡ぐ繊細なハーモニー。
lines.english: Delicate harmonies, woven as the two cherish each other.

lines.japanese: ほどよい甘さは不健康な色気を感じさせず、たとえれば懐かしい日の夢を見ているような、温もりのクオリア。
lines.english: Just sweet enough, without any unhealthy sensuality. Like dreaming of a day from long ago: the qualia of warmth.

lines.japanese: 漠然と……ランドセルを背負っていたころの登校風景がよみがえった。
lines.english: Vaguely... I remember the walk to school with my satchel on my back.

lines.japanese: 見送る祖母の手。
lines.english: My grandmother's hand waving me off.

lines.japanese: すこし重い習字道具。
lines.english: The slightly heavy calligraphy supplies.

lines.japanese: 給食当番の白衣。
lines.english: The white coat for serving school lunch.

lines.japanese: お向かいのみよちゃん。
lines.english: Miyo from across the street.

lines.japanese: 図工が得意なさっちゃん。
lines.english: Satch, good at arts and crafts.

lines.japanese: はしゃいでる私。
lines.english: Me, having fun.

lines.japanese: きのう観たテレビの話。
lines.english: Talking about yesterday's TV.

lines.japanese: 新しいゴム跳びの技。
lines.english: A new rubber-band jumping trick.

lines.japanese: お菓子みたいな消しゴムの臭い。
lines.english: The candy-like smell of erasers.

lines.japanese: 体育帽のゴムの味。
lines.english: The taste of my gym cap's elastic.

lines.japanese: 鼻を衝きぬけるプールの水。
lines.english: Pool water shooting through my nose.

lines.japanese: はしゃいでる私。
lines.english: Me, having fun.

lines.japanese: 放課後の約束。
lines.english: Plans for after school.

lines.japanese: 大勢の友達。
lines.english: Lots of friends.

lines.japanese: はしゃいでる私。
lines.english: Me, having fun.

lines.japanese: あのころは楽しかったな。
lines.english: I had fun back then.

lines.japanese: 楽しかったな。
lines.english: I had fun.

lines.japanese: 毎日はしゃいでた気がするな。
lines.english: I think I played and laughed every day.

lines.japanese: スカートが翻るのも気にしないで、毎日くるくるはしゃいでた気がするな。
lines.english: I think I whirled around having fun every day, not even caring if my skirt flipped up.

lines.japanese: 「ふふ」
lines.english: “Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 伸びる歩道はずっとまっすぐ。私は目を閉じたまま、のどかな旋律に合わせてゆっくりと歩きだした。
lines.english: The sidewalk stretches straight ahead. Eyes still closed, I begin walking slowly to the peaceful melody.

lines.japanese: ときに音楽は耳から入れるトランキライザー。向精神薬をスニッフするより安全・確実・効果てきめん。
lines.english: Sometimes music is a tranquilizer taken through the ears. Safer, more reliable, and more immediately effective than snorting psychiatric drugs.

lines.japanese: 誰をも傷付けないひたすら優しい音色が私を取りまいて、ここではないどこかへと運んでくれる。
lines.english: Nothing but gentle tones that hurt no one surround me and carry me somewhere that isn't here.

lines.japanese: 私は私の身体を離れ、たゆたう音のさざ波に身を任せていた。
lines.english: I leave my body and surrender to the drifting ripples of sound.

lines.japanese: 前、前、休み……前、前、後ろ……
lines.english: Front, front, rest... front, front, back...

lines.japanese: まーえ、休み、休み……まーえ、前、前……
lines.english: Fro-ont, rest, rest... fro-ont, front, front...

lines.japanese: 謡うように、踊るように。
lines.english: As if singing, as if dancing.

lines.japanese: 揺れるように、舞うように。
lines.english: As if swaying, as if floating.

lines.japanese: 憂鬱な朝、心地よい音楽だけが私を灰色の重力から解きはなつ。
lines.english: On a gloomy morning, pleasant music alone frees me from the gray gravity.

lines.japanese: 右、左、中……まーえ、休み、まーえ……！
lines.english: Right, left, middle... fro-ont, rest, fro-ont...!

lines.japanese: ジャンプ、前、前……くるっ、トントン……！
lines.english: Jump, front, front... spin, tap-tap...!

lines.japanese: 「おかあさーん、あれなーにー」
lines.english: “Mommy, what's that?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「シッ、見るんじゃありません！」
lines.english: “Shh! Don't look!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああう……」
lines.english: “Ah, aagh...”

lines.japanese: 恥ずかしいと感じるのは体調が良い証拠──
lines.english: Feeling embarrassed is a sign that I'm doing well—

lines.japanese: ──と自分を慰めながら早足でその場を逃げだした。
lines.english: —I comfort myself with that thought as I hurry away.

lines.japanese: 「えー、それじゃあ一週間分、出しておきましょうねー」
lines.english: “Um, then, I'll give you a week's worth, all right?”

lines.japanese: クリニックへ着くころには普段どおり話せるようになっていて、診察も滞りなく終わった。
lines.english: By the time I reach the clinic, I can talk as usual, and the appointment ends without difficulty.

lines.japanese: 「えー、頓服のもの以外に関してはね、えー、もし調子が良くても、ご自分の判断で飲むのやめちゃったりとかね、そういうことないようにお願いしますね」
lines.english: “Um, apart from the ones you take as needed, um, even if you're feeling well, please don't decide on your own to stop taking them. Things like that. All right?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。ありがとうございました、失礼します」
lines.english: “Yes. Thank you very much. Goodbye.”

lines.japanese: 会計を済ませて外へ出た。
lines.english: I pay and go outside.

lines.japanese: 受けとった処方箋をさっそく確認してみる。昔はまるで暗号としか思えなかった記述も、今では普通に理解できるほど慣れ親しんでしまった。
lines.english: I immediately check the prescription I've received. What once looked like code has become so familiar that I can now read it without any trouble.

lines.japanese: 「……正夢か」
lines.english: “...So the dream came true.”

lines.japanese: 予想通りの処方だった。
lines.english: The prescription is exactly what I expected.
“Oh.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 前方から声がしたので、顔を上げた。
lines.english: A voice ahead makes me lift my head.

lines.japanese: 「お、おお」
lines.english: “Oh, uh, hey.”

lines.japanese: 去年同じクラスだった、もり……もりさと君。下の名前は忘れた。その程度の関係。学校でもほとんど話したことがなく、過去に一度この診療所の待合室で鉢合わせたことがあるだけだ。
lines.english: Mori... Morisato, who was in my class last year. I've forgotten his first name. That's how little we know each other. We hardly ever talked at school. We've only run into each other once before in this clinic's waiting room.

lines.japanese: 彼は私が出てきたビルに、人差し指を向けながら言った。
lines.english: Pointing at the building I've just left, he speaks.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　行ってきたん？」
lines.english: “Hm? You just went?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。そう」
lines.english: “Yeah. I did.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……ああ、俺は、いまから」
lines.english: “Huh... Oh, I'm going now.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。ふうん」
lines.english: “Oh, okay. Hmm.”

lines.japanese: あまり知った顔には会いたくない場所という認識があるのだろう、前回会ったときもそうだったけど、今日も森里君の歯切れは悪かった。
lines.english: He probably sees it as somewhere he'd rather not meet anyone he knows. Last time was the same. Today, Morisato is stumbling over his words again.

lines.japanese: 私の記憶が正しければ、教室での彼は、つねに茶化しやおどけや冷やかしばかりを口にしているようなタイプだったはずだ。
lines.english: If I remember right, in class he was the sort who was always joking, clowning, and making fun of things.

lines.japanese: 「あの、やっぱ、早い時間のが予約取りやすいとか……ああ、あんのかな」
lines.english: “Um, is it, like, easier to get an appointment early in the day... Uh, is that a thing?”

lines.japanese: そのまま通りすぎるものと思ったけど、意外や森里君は足を止めて、落ちつきなく頭を掻きながら言った。
lines.english: I thought he'd just walk past, but unexpectedly, Morisato stops, scratching his head restlessly.

lines.japanese: そういえば私も通院しだしたころは、ネットで同類を探しもとめるほどに不安を抱えていたものだ。私は彼に合わせて明度を調整する。明度というのはこの場合──
lines.english: Come to think of it, when I first started coming here, I was anxious enough to search online for others like me. I adjust my brightness to match his. Brightness, in this case, means—

lines.japanese: 「あ、アレ？　やっぱ山科も、あの、保健室のおばちゃんに勧められて？」
lines.english: “Oh, hey? You too, Yamashina? Uh, the lady in the nurse's office recommended it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そんな感じ。実は結構いるよ、診療内科行ったことある子。すぐ良くなっちゃうから目立たないだけで」
lines.english: “Yeah, something like that. Actually, quite a few kids have been to a mental-health clinic. They just get better quickly, so you don't notice.”

lines.japanese: 私はセオリー通りの対応をした。自分が二年以上通院してることは伏せておいた。
lines.english: I respond by the book. I don't mention that I've been coming for more than two years.

lines.japanese: 「へえ……あ、はあ、そーゆーもんなんだ？」
lines.english: “Huh... Oh, right. So that's how it is?”

lines.japanese: はたして森里君は、落ちつきを取りもどしたかのように両手をポケットへ収めて笑った。
lines.english: Sure enough, Morisato puts both hands in his pockets and smiles, as if he's recovered his composure.

lines.japanese: 「ま、だよな？　だって実際、山科がこーゆトコ出入りしてるなんて、俺ら誰も知らなかったもんなあ？」
lines.english: “Well, yeah, right? I mean, none of us actually knew you were coming to a place like this.”

lines.japanese: あ、なるほど、そこを気にしてるのか。だったら安心させてあげよう。
lines.english: Oh, I see. That's what he's worried about. Then I'll reassure him.

lines.japanese: 「うん。私も森里君のこと言わないよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I won't tell anyone about you either.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、マジ？　ハハ、悪りいね、ありゃーとぁーっす。んじゃー、そんな感じで。ちょっす、またね」
lines.english: “Oh, for real? Ha ha, sorry about that. Much 'preciated! A'right, then. See ya.”

lines.japanese: ちゃっ、と敬礼の真似をして、彼はクリニックのビルへひょいひょい駆けていった。
lines.english: With a quick little imitation of a salute, he jogs off toward the clinic building.

lines.japanese: 「くすっ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: 私はその背中を見送りながら、達観した先人を気取って呟いてみた。
lines.english: Watching him go, I murmur, playing the worldly-wise veteran.

lines.japanese: 「昭和じゃないんだから……いまどきメンヘル通いぐらい、珍しくもないでしょう」
lines.english: “It’s not the Showa era anymore... Going to a mental-health clinic isn’t that unusual these days.”

lines.japanese: だけど励ましてもらったのはお互いさまみたいだ。
lines.english: But it seems we both gave each other some encouragement.

lines.japanese: 私は口笛を吹きながら学校へ向かった。
lines.english: I head for school, whistling.
